page.overview:
Who is Gong-gong?

He raised Jin in Ba Sing Se and taught her calligraphy so that she might get a chance to escape poverty through education. These efforts resulted in Jin getting a scholarship for a literature academy. Yet Gong-gong began to suffer from a mental illness which resulted in bouts of confusion of growing frequency. After suffering a heart attack during the Fire Nation conquest of Ba Sing Se, he eventually died, using his last lucid moments to express his pride in his granddaughter.

A member of the Guan family of the Earth Kingdom, and became known for his mastery of the Duanshan writing style. Upon returning to his home village, he continued to hone his craft

At one point, Gong-gong had a daughter named Biyu. Biyu eventually fell in love with and married a young scholar from Omashu. Gong-gong strongly approved of his son-in-law due to the latter's character and profession. When his son-in-law was appointed village magistrate of Daying, Gong-gong accompanied his family to settle there. He continued to be somewhat frustrated over his daughter, however, as she enlisted as a soldier in Daying's garrison. Meanwhile, Gong-gong set up his own study in Daying and garnered a very positive reputation for his work. He even started working for the regional governor, writing texts for the local official to be delivered to the Earth Kingdom capital.

When his granddaughter Jin was born in Daying, Gong-gong became very close to her and often cared for her. In contrast to her mother, Jin also showed interest in calligraphy, resulting in the older man starting to teach her from an early age. Gong-gong hoped that Jin might one day continue her family's climb of the social ladder and perhaps become a local governor.
